title: Just-in-Time Ontologies: What Cheap Intelligence Means for Data — Hrishi Olickel, Southbridge AI
talk_summary: The speaker argues there is no universal schema; useful transformations are built just-in-time around a decision, using cheap models as workers and stronger models for design/optimization. He shows a data pipeline where role-split models, cross-family disagreement checks, bounded pilots, a checkpointed harness, and Pareto model swapping cut a projected $10k job to $795.

takeaways.what_they_do: Separate pipeline design/planning from in-pipeline execution; use slower heavy models for design and cheap fast specialized models for repeatable worker steps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The first one wants slower models with heavier, thicker tokens, models that can think more

takeaways.what_they_do: Run two different model families on the same review/QA task; trust agreement, escalate only disagreements to stronger or human review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Jev and Luna agreed on 194. And none of those shared answers was wrong. Every error sat in the six families where they disagree.

takeaways.what_they_do: Define a measurable failure surface and baseline on a small checked slice before starting; use bounded pilots before scaling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's very important to have to define a failure surface before you ever start

takeaways.technique: Checkpointed harness with rollback and budget enforcement
takeaways.what_they_do: Put agent runs behind a stable harness/API with checkpointing, rollback, budget enforcement, and logs; reuse validated segments.
takeaways.evidence_quote: consistent, well-tested log and API interface with checkpointing, rollback, budget enforcement, everything built in

takeaways.what_they_do: Start from a working baseline, swap models/components for cheaper/faster options, compare against known intermediate outputs, and tighten the success threshold.
takeaways.evidence_quote: swap models and some other parts for faster and cheaper options, compare against known intermediates, tighten the requirement for success
takeaways.numbers: $795 on $800 budget vs ~$10,000 expected; checking $545 vs first answers $128

takeaways.what_they_do: When a cheap model misses, clarify question definitions and evidence criteria in the prompt; version and reuse prompt changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we rewrote the questions. Without touching the models of the thresholds, the household question now said what counts as enough evidence
takeaways.numbers: 13 development questions changed from no to yes
